inicio.titulo: Trusting what AI builds: the basics for anyone who will help companies adopt AI
inicio.lead: Building with AI got cheap. Trusting what it builds is still expensive. In eight lessons, you learn what AI does well, build a small app and look for flaws in it, recognize the risks that sink projects, and write a one-pager the board understands.
inicio.capa_alt: Trusting what AI builds — Professional 2030, Common Core. A professional examines an app on a laptop with a magnifying glass.
inicio.aulas_sub: In order: understand, build, find the risk, decide on data and rules, say what you are not, and talk to the board.

itens: Any professional who will help a company adopt AI with method and safety, even without knowing how to code.
Anyone who wants to follow one of the four Professional 2030 tracks: it is the recommended prerequisite (not required).
Anyone who already uses AI at work and wants to know where it goes wrong before trusting it.

blocos.t: What you walk away able to do
itens: Say, for a given task, whether AI does it well, does it with checking, or should not do it.
Build a one-screen app with AI and find three flaws in it.
Recognize an exposed key, prompt injection, too many permissions, and action without approval.
Decide where a piece of data can go and build the timeline of the rules.
Hand the board a one-page diagnosis.
This course is the Common Core of Professional 2030, an open INEMA program. Each track will have INEMA certification; details soon. It is a qualification certificate, not a regulated profession.
